telegram.about: Messages come from your own Telegram bot, made with @BotFather.

help.bot_token: Given by @BotFather, like 123456789:AAH… Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.chat_id: A user or group id, or @channel. Add the bot to the group first.
help.topic_id: Only for a group with topics: the number of the topic that receives the messages.

gotify.about: Your Gotify server: create an application there and copy its token.

help.server: For example https://gotify.example.org. On your home network, tick “Allow a private-network destination”.
help.token: The token of the application (not a client token). Write-only: it is never shown again.

home_assistant.about: Sends to a Home Assistant notify service, with a long-lived access token.

help.url: For example http://homeassistant.local:8123, without a path such as /ha. On your home network, tick “Allow a private-network destination”.
help.token: Profile, Security, Long-lived access tokens. Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.service: The service name, for example mobile_app_your_phone.

pushover.about: Create an application on pushover.net, then copy its token and your user key.

help.user_key: Shown on your Pushover dashboard (30 characters). Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.app_token: The API token of the application you created (30 characters). Write-only: it is never shown again.
help.devices: Device names separated by commas (up to 10). Empty: every device of your account.

matrix.about: Posts to a Matrix room with a dedicated account that joined it.

help.server: For example https://matrix.example.org, without a path. On your home network, tick “Allow a private-network destination”.
help.username: Leave empty with an access token.
help.credential: An access token or the account password. Never shown again.

signal.about: Sends through a signal-cli REST API server you host.

help.server: For example http://signal-api.lan:8080, without a path. On your home network, tick “Allow a private-network destination”.
help.from_number: The number registered in signal-cli, with its country code: +33600000000.
help.to: Numbers in international format, separated by commas (10 at most).
help.password: Only if a proxy protects the server. Never shown again.

slack.about: Posts to the channel of a Slack incoming webhook.

help.webhook: The https://hooks.slack.com/services/… address Slack gives you. Never shown again.

mattermost.about: Posts to the channel of a Mattermost incoming webhook. Messages use Markdown.

help.server: For example https://mattermost.example.org. On your home network, tick “Allow a private-network destination”.
help.token: The last part of the webhook address (…/hooks/<key>). Write-only: it is never shown again.

rocketchat.about: Posts to a Rocket.Chat room as a dedicated account that has joined it.

help.server: For example https://chat.example.org, without a path. On your home network, tick “Allow a private-network destination”.
help.password: The password or a personal access token. Never shown again.
help.room: A channel (#general), a user (@name) or a room id.
help.username: The user name, or the user ID with a token.

sms_free.about: Sends a text to your own Free Mobile line. Only a short title is sent.

help.api_key: The key shown when you enable the option. Write-only: it is never shown again.

sms_sfr.about: Sends texts through SFR's SMS API. Only a short title is sent.

help.username: The login of your SFR messaging account.
help.space_id: The space (service) identifier given by SFR for your account.
help.to: One or more numbers with their country code, separated by commas (up to 10): +33600000000.
